text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Serving runtime error spike on prod-us-west continuous-batcher (severity: P1). Error: GPU OOM + worker crashes. See dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/2134567890 :rotating_light:

alice: noticing 5xxs and latency >5s for /v1/generate starting ~2134567820. Root says batch queue depth creeping.

raj: I'm on it, looking at the batcher logs now.

alice: stack: `cudaRuntimeMalloc` followed by `std::bad_alloc` in the runtime, repeated across 6 replicas. Pod restarts 3x in last 10m.

raj: logs snippet:
```
E 13:11:12 runtime.cpp:412] CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 18446744073709551615 bytes
W 13:11:12 batcher.cpp:219] batch growth: qlen=462, avg_seq=2048, inflight=37
I 13:11:12 healthcheck: failing
```

sasha: that's huge qlen. Did autoscaler kick?

ops-bot: Autoscaler: no new nodes created. Reason: quota cap at region us-west-2 reached.

jeff: customer-impact: 3 customers report timeouts for document summarization flows. Ticket #INC-4821 created.

maria: I'm pausing new canary traffic via routing rule to stable-1 for impacted models. Setting weight 0.

alice: mitigation plan: 1) throttle admission (limit inflight per model), 2) reduce max_batch_size env on replicas, 3) restart unhealthy replicas in controlled churn, 4) escalate capacity request.

raj: applying quick throttle: `kubectl exec deploy/batcher -- /bin/sh -c "echo 40 > /proc/sys/batcher/max_inflight"` — pushing now.

oncall-bot: @raj assigned (oncall). Estimated ETA for config change to take effect: 15s.

raj: changed max_inflight to 40. Observing qlen dropping from 462 -> 220 over 45s. Latency trending down.

alice: good. But still seeing CUDA OOMs in the oldest pod (batcher-5). Might be KV cache growth in long-running processes.

jeff: suggestion: soft-restart of pods one-by-one to clear KV cache. Use `kubectl rollout restart deploy/batcher -n prod --field-selector metadata.name=batcher-...` carefully.

maria: doing controlled restart: rollingRestart.sh invoked with `maxUnavailable=1` and `preStop` sleep 5s. Starting now.

ops-bot: Restart initiated: batcher-3 -> terminated, batcher-3 recreated.

alice: healthchecks back to passing for restarted pods. No OOMs seen in new pods.

raj: but now seeing a deadlock between admission controller and queue monitor: admission stops accepting small requests intermittently -> queue starvation for low-latency traffic.

sasha: can you paste the admission traces?

raj: trace:
```
I 13:12:40 admission.cpp:enter checkAdmission(model=llama-xt, tokens=64)
D 13:12:40 kvcache.cpp:evictBatch() -> waiting on mutex
I 13:12:41 admission.cpp:blocked waiting on cache
I 13:12:42 queue_monitor.cpp:observed qlen=5 ser=low, but inflight=120
```

alice: so the cache eviction mutex held by a long-running quantization flush during restart. That blocks admission and small requests get starved while big queued batches consume memory -> intermittent latency spikes.

jeff: customer-impact update: extended to 12 customers, mostly low-rate latency-sensitive endpoints. I'll update INC-4821.

maria: interim: enabling admission backpressure override for latency tier: `ADMISSION_OVERRIDES=latency:allow=0.2` — reduces prioritized take for long-batch jobs. Applying now.

raj: override applied. small requests processing rate improved, error rate for low-latency models dropped by 70%.

alice: ops ask: request quota bump submitted to cloud team for us-west-2 (+2 GPUs) — ticket CLOUD-1198. Status: pending approval.

sasha: while we wait for capacity, we should patch runtime to avoid holding eviction mutex for >50ms. I can push a hotfix to make eviction incremental.

raj: agreed. Can you author and test a micro-patch? Keep change minimal: replace single locked eviction with chunked loop and yield.

sasha: pushing branch `hotfix/incremental-evict`. Test plan: unit + staging load test with synthetic burst.

oncall-bot: @sasha assigned. ETA 30m for patch + canary.

jeff: public comms: add status page note: "We are mitigating a performance regression causing timeouts for some API calls; workaround in place, investigating root cause." I'll post once we have confirmation of stabilization.

maria: after throttle + restart + admission override: system stabilized around 2134567980. Error rate back to baseline by 2134568020.

alice: final summary for timeline (for postmortem):
- 2134567820: latency increase reported.
- 2134567850: GPU OOMs began on several replicas.
- 2134567880: incident declared P1.
- 2134567900: admission throttle applied.
- 2134567920: rolling restarts to reclaim KV caches.
- 2134567955: admission override for latency traffic applied.
- 2134567980: major error rate reduced.
- 2134568020: baseline recovered.

raj: adding follow-ups: 1) cap KV cache size per replica, 2) make eviction incremental (sasha), 3) autoscaler quota alerting improvements (ops), 4) add model-level admission SLA settings for low-latency customers.

sasha: will PR hotfix within 45m.

jeff: I'll update INC-4821 and send a customer note to impacted accounts with mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: status -> mitigated (P1 -> P2) at 2134568030.

maria: handing off to evening oncall: @jeff will own follow-ups.

jeff: ack, I'll pick up the follow-ups and drive the postmortem.

alice: thanks team. We'll capture RCA: continuous-batcher eviction + admission coupling + capacity limits + restart policy = combined failure.

ops-bot: Cleanup tasks queued: CLOUD-1198, INC-4821, SRE-2372, HOTFIX-871.

oncall-bot: thread closed for now. If regressions appear, re-open with new alert. :white_check_mark:
